reason: The hypothesis directly restates the core finding of P1—that RTA-induced anisotropic strain and directional chemical order in fcc FeCoNiMnCu films cause a large coercivity increase—and applies it to FeCoNi with an externally applied tensile strain, which is a minor modification of the same mechanism and predicted outcome. The idea of using strain to induce low-symmetry ordering for higher coercivity is explicitly proposed as future work in P5 and P6, and the mechanism is taken word for word from P1 and P7.
copied_elements: RTA-induced strain and directional chemical order boost coercivity (P1)
Microstructural distortions impede domain wall motion, increasing coercivity (P7)
Low-symmetry ordering (L10) enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy (P5, P6)
Coercivity increase from <100 Oe to >300 Oe mirrors P1's 40-fold increase
Falsification via coercivity increase and structural analysis is standard practice
